policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's main text, 'loose thyself from the bonds of thy neck,' renders the qere's feminine singular imperative; the mapped textual-variant note explicitly assigns the passive reading 'the bonds of thy neck are loosed' only as another reading.
ASV 'what do I here' distinguishes the qere מַה לִּי ('what [is] to me/here') from the ketiv מי לי ('who [is] for me').
ASV 'they that rule over them' expresses the pronominal object 'over them,' distinguishing the qere מֹשְׁלָיו from the ketiv משלו.
